newsitem.title: CANADA: Northstar to drill at contentious location.
newsitem.headline: Northstar to drill at contentious location.

text.p: Northstar Energy Corp said on Monday it planned to drill another natural gas well at an Alberta foothills location that became contentious during Canadian 88 Energy Corp's failed bid for Morrison Petroleums Ltd in January.

Northstar, which merged with Morrison in a friendly C$700-million deal after Canadian 88 scrapped its controversial hostile bid, said it would drill a third well at Racehorce Creek in southwestern Alberta.
The company said it believed the first two wells missed the richest part of the geological structure.

As an independent firm, Morrison drilled two deep and expensive wells at Racehorse, but technical problems led to disappointing results, no production and a skid in the firm's stock price late last year.
Morrison's share price drop opened the door to the bid from Canadian 88, whose chief executive, Greg Noval, sharply criticized Morrison's technical staff for the drilling problems at Racehorse.

Northstar chief executive John Hagg said the new Racehorse well, located in the Alberta region known for expensive and complex drilling and potentially rich gas reserves, was being viewed as a development well despite its high-risk nature.

"I mean, a hundred petroleum engineers would look at the data to date and say there's gas there," Hagg said in a phone interview. "It's a question of how productive it is and what are the rates that it will produce at."

Logs from the first two wells showed the Racehorce prospect had three productive geological zones with highly fractured rock. The new location's success would depend on how well the location was picked from the well logs and earlier seismic data, he said.

Northstar, which earlier reported a big jump in first-quarter earnings after a non-recurring gain, said it booked 16 billion cubic feet of proven and 26 BCF of probable gas reserves from the first two wells after the merger.
Northstar's 50-50 partner in the prospect is Norcen Energy Resources Ltd.

Meanwhile, Hagg said he believed several factors had led to Northstar's lackluster stock market performance following the merger with Morrison, including a negative reaction from arbitragers who held Morrison stock before share swap deal.
Investors had also been unsure of Northstar's progress in merging the two organizations, he said.

Northstar shares on Monday were trading down 0.15 to 12.05, their lowest level since the merger was announced in early February. The stock had climbed to 15.15 on February 18, but has been mostly falling since.
"Our job is to simply prove to the market that we're successfully pulling these companies together and that we're building a company here that is going to be able to grow into the future," Hagg said.

He said Northstar's target was to complete the merger process -- which still included putting both staffs into the same building and melding different accounting and land systems -- by the end of the second quarter.
Northstar earlier reported first-quarter net earnings of C$37.9 million or C$0.41 a share, up from C$11.7 million or C$0.14 a share in the same period last year.
